title: Rockall Score (Upper GI Bleed)
sources: Rockall TA et al. Gut 1996; NICE NG12 acute UGIB guidance
purpose: Predicts mortality and rebleeding after an acute upper GI bleed. The first three items give the PRE-endoscopy (clinical) Rockall; adding the last two gives the FULL (post-endoscopy) Rockall. Use Glasgow-Blatchford for the pre-endoscopy decision about who can go home — Rockall's strength is post-endoscopy prognosis.

options.label: Cardiac failure, ischaemic heart disease, or any major comorbidity
Renal failure, liver failure, or disseminated malignancy
Mallory-Weiss tear or no lesion identified, and no stigmata of recent haemorrhage
Malignancy of the upper GI tract
Blood in the upper GI tract, adherent clot, visible or spurting vessel

interpretation.label: Low risk — full Rockall ≤ 2 predicts rebleeding ~ 5% and mortality ~ 0–1%. A pre-endoscopy (clinical) Rockall of 0 with a Glasgow-Blatchford of 0 supports outpatient management
Intermediate risk — rebleeding ~ 11–24%, mortality ~ 3–11%. Admit; inpatient endoscopy within 24 h, monitored bed if unstable
High risk — rebleeding ~ 33–41%, mortality ~ 17–41%. Urgent endoscopy, ICU / HDU, aggressive resuscitation and transfusion, early surgical / IR involvement for uncontrolled bleeding

notes: Pre-endoscopy Rockall uses only age + shock + comorbidity (max 7). Do not use Rockall to select patients for discharge without endoscopy — that is the Glasgow-Blatchford score's role (GBS 0–1 = candidate for outpatient management). Give a PPI infusion for high-risk stigmata; resuscitate to a restrictive Hb target ~ 7 g/dL unless active massive bleeding or cardiovascular disease.
buildNote: Additive. Pre-endoscopy = first 3 items (max 7); full = all 5 (max 11).
